accuracy.evidence: Checked against NOAA Tsunami Program ('Tsunami Facts', 'Tsunami Safety'), USGS 'Life of a Tsunami', BGS 'Tsunamis' and the UNESCO IOC Tsunami Glossary: most tsunamis are generated by large undersea earthquakes that displace the sea floor, others by submarine landslides and volcanic eruptions; wind and tides do not generate them, so 'tidal wave' is a misnomer. Speeds computed from c = √(g·d): 4,000 m gives 198 m/s ≈ 713 km/h (stated 'about 700 km/h, as fast as a jet plane'), 100 m gives 31 m/s ≈ 113 km/h (about 110), 10 m gives 9.9 m/s ≈ 36 km/h (about 35). Deep-water amplitude under 1 m and shoaling growth match NOAA; natural warnings (strong or long shaking, sea drawback, roar) and 'go to high ground or inland, stay until officials say it is safe; later waves can be larger' match NOAA and IOC guidance.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented ideas (NOAA/ITIC education guidance; studies after the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami on people walking out onto the exposed sea floor): tides or wind cause tsunamis (step 1 predict, cause sort, Ann, Col, tags tide and wind), a tsunami is a wall of water out at sea (Dee, m2, tag tall), it is fastest near the beach (step 3 predict, wrong-tap message, tag slow), the sea drawing back is harmless low tide (step 4 predict, 'Walk out to look', 'Pick up the fish'), and it is a single wave so it is safe after the first (Gia, Ida, m4, tag back).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). The prerequisite What Is an Earthquake and 583 Earthquake Safety (flagearthq, Drop-Cover-Hold) cover shaking on land; 108 flagwave and 673 flagtide cover ordinary waves and tides. This lab pushes a block of sea floor to lift the water column and split it into two travelling humps, then orders places on a shoaling sea profile by depth-controlled speed and height; neither mechanism appears in another lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Pushing the sea floor makes the water surface above rise by the same shape and then spread both ways, so 'the whole sea is pushed, not just the top' is seen. Tapping places from fastest to slowest is checked against depth, and each correct tap draws the wave at that place (tiny in the deep ocean, tall near the beach) with its speed and a comparison, so 'deep and fast, shallow and tall' is discovered before the summary. The safety task responds to each wrong choice with the danger it causes.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options that the tasks disprove: 'Strong wind' or 'The tide' as the start, 'Nothing, the sea is too deep' when the floor jumps, 'Near the beach' as the fastest place, and 'It is just low tide' for the sea rushing out. A.reveal reports each prediction against the result.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged wrong answers and their own messages: wind (wind only stirs the top), tide (tides rise and fall daily; tsunamis come from the floor, a landslide or a volcano), slow (fastest where deepest), tall (low out at sea, under 1 m), look (never go to look) and back (more waves for hours, later ones can be bigger). Lab mistakes are named too, e.g. 'Not yet. The wave is faster where the sea is deeper. Deep ocean: 4,000 m deep. Near the beach: only 10 m deep.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons readability passed (kid under 6.5, adult under 9.5). Kid paragraphs are short and use the terms tsunami, earthquake, sea floor, deep ocean and shallow. Canvas text is one instruction per step and buttons say what they do (Push the sea floor up, Deep ocean, Warning sign, Run to high ground now, Hal is right).

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and explanation similarity under 12% to all lessons. Each kid paragraph carries one idea (what starts it; low and fast at sea; slow and tall near land; warnings and staying high). The adult text gives curriculum links, sourced speeds, the six tasks and named slips.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of all seven steps before and after Show me (/workspace/wn-run-1116-2352/shots/ts-*). After the first pass the sea floor sat on the bottom edge and the block was a sliver, so the profile was raised with a sand layer underneath and the block made wider and taller. Sort cards, bins, the three place markers (52 px tap areas) and the choice cards span the width and stay above the feedback box.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all six tasks complete with Show me, challenge shown, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors. Every drag or tap has a button (Can start a tsunami / Cannot, Push the sea floor up, Deep ocean / Edge of the land / Near the beach, Warning sign / Not a sign, each safety choice, '<name> is right'), and the canvas aria-label gives the card being sorted, the floor lift, each place's depth and the order so far.
